summary: Cedar Butte lookout, Tillamook County: 1937 tower, 1939 L-4 tower after a fire, 1955 duties moved to Triangulation Point; now demolished, with a short hike to the former site.

facts.status_note: The 1939 L-4 tower is gone. Oregon Hikers reports the demolished cabin left glass shards on the site. The weebly list says removed, with no date.

access.note: Listed by Oregon Hikers as a short hike to the former lookout site. No closure is noted in the sources.

visit.trail_note: Oregon Hikers lists a short, steep hike of 1.6 miles with 780 ft of gain to the former site. No tower remains to climb.

facts.agency: Northwest Oregon FPA/OFD (per FFLOS); Oregon Department of Forestry (per weebly and firelookout.com)

events.note: Sources differ on the first structure: rag camp and pole platform (FFLOS), crow's nest and cabin (firelookout.com), observation point (weebly).
Newspaper report that a lookout would be established on Cedar Butte in the 1933 burn area.
40-foot tower and cab. FFLOS calls it a 40' pole live-in tower.
Alfred Hastings was the lookout, per The Forest Log, September 1937.
FFLOS says the 1937 tower was destroyed by a forest fire in 1938. Oregon Hikers dates a fire that hit the lookout to 1939, without naming the tower.
New 40-foot tower with a 14x14 L-4 cab, per the weebly page. FFLOS says a 40' pole L-4 tower was constructed.
Oregon Hikers says the fire lookout became a victim of one of the massive fires of the 1930s and 1940s in 1939.
Trask fire. Gene Scott, Cedar Butte lookout, reported to have escaped a ring of fire by swimming and wading four miles down the Wilson River.
Lookout activated for the Portland Filter Center on March 18, 1942.
Lookout duties transferred to the new lookout at Triangulation Point. This is a change of duty, not a removal date.
Registered with the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register on September 23, 2010.

corrections.why: Both FFLOS and the weebly page describe a 40-foot tower with an L-4 cab built in 1939. The record's ground kind does not match the 1939 structure. The 1917 structure may have been a ground-level platform, so check the 1917 form.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS gives a rag camp and pole platform in 1917. firelookout.com gives a crow's nest and cabin. The weebly page gives an observation point. The story reports all three and does not choose one.

FFLOS dates the fire that destroyed the 1937 tower to 1938. Oregon Hikers dates a fire that hit the lookout to 1939 and does not name the tower. The story gives both dates and does not assume they are the same fire.

notes_for_editor: The 1937-1939 sequence conflicts across FFLOS, the weebly page and Oregon Hikers; the story reports the conflict. The removal date is not given in any read source. A web search snippet claimed the lookout was dismantled in the early 1950s and a Hiking Project page claimed demolition with broken glass; neither was read in full, so neither is used. The 1955 date is the transfer of duties to Triangulation Point, not a removal date. The agency is OFD in FFLOS and ODF in the other sources. The kind correction (ground to tower) needs an editor check against the 1917 form.
